subproblem.title: Gram matrix of a linear map: symmetric, positive semidefinite, with trace |D|^2
subproblem.statement: For all natural numbers n, l and every continuous linear map D : R^n -> R^l (D : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ), let e_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1 (a in Fin n) be the standard basis of R^n and let G be the real n x n matrix G_ab := <D e_a, D e_b> (Matrix.of fun a b => inner ℝ (D e_a) (D e_b)). Then (i) G is symmetric, G^T = G (Matrix.IsSymm G); (ii) for every x : Fin n -> R the quadratic form x . (G x) = sum_a x_a sum_b G_ab x_b (dotProduct x (Matrix.mulVec G x)) is >= 0; (iii) trace G = sum_a G_aa equals hsNormSq D = sum_a |D e_a|^2.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (D : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ), Matrix.IsSymm (Matrix.of fun a b : Fin n => inner ℝ (D (EuclideanSpace.single a (1 : ℝ))) (D (EuclideanSpace.single b (1 : ℝ)))) ∧ (∀ x : Fin n → ℝ, 0 ≤ dotProduct x (Matrix.mulVec (Matrix.of fun a b : Fin n => inner ℝ (D (EuclideanSpace.single a (1 : ℝ))) (D (EuclideanSpace.single b (1 : ℝ)))) x)) ∧ Matrix.trace (Matrix.of fun a b : Fin n => inner ℝ (D (EuclideanSpace.single a (1 : ℝ))) (D (EuclideanSpace.single b (1 : ℝ)))) = hsNormSq D
subproblem.natural_proof:
Context. This child is the Gram-matrix half of steps 1, 2 and 6 of the parent proof. It shows that G = (<D e_a, D e_b>) is symmetric and positive semidefinite, which are the hypotheses of the sibling gwe_gjb_det_one_add_bounds. It also shows trace G = hsNormSq D, which lets the parent rewrite exp(trace G) as exp(hsNormSq D).

Notation.
- e_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1 is the a-th standard basis vector of R^n = EuclideanSpace R (Fin n).
- v_a := D e_a, a vector in R^l.
- G := Matrix.of (fun a b => <v_a, v_b>), so G_ab = <v_a, v_b> (Matrix.of_apply).
- For x, y : Fin n -> R, dotProduct x y = sum_i x_i y_i, and (Matrix.mulVec G x)_a = sum_b G_ab x_b. Over R there is no conjugation.
- The inner product on R^l = EuclideanSpace R (Fin l) is the real Euclidean one. It is bilinear and symmetric, and <w, w> = ||w||^2 >= 0.

1. Symmetry (i). Matrix.IsSymm G means G^T = G. By matrix extensionality it suffices to show (G^T)_ab = G_ab for all a, b. Indeed (G^T)_ab = G_ba = <v_b, v_a> = <v_a, v_b> = G_ab, by symmetry of the real inner product (real_inner_comm).
2. Expanding the quadratic form (ii). Fix x : Fin n -> R. By the definitions of dotProduct and mulVec, after distributing x_a over the inner sum,
   x . (G x) = sum_a x_a (sum_b <v_a, v_b> x_b) = sum_a sum_b x_a x_b <v_a, v_b>.
3. Let w := sum_a x_a • v_a in R^l. By bilinearity of the real inner product (sum_inner, inner_sum, inner_smul_left, inner_smul_right; conjugation is trivial over R),
   <w, w> = sum_a sum_b x_a x_b <v_a, v_b>.
   If the expansion yields <v_b, v_a> in the (a, b) summand, rewrite it to <v_a, v_b> with real_inner_comm. The scalar factors then agree by commutativity of multiplication.
4. By steps 2 and 3, x . (G x) = <w, w> >= 0 (real_inner_self_nonneg).
5. Trace (iii). Matrix.trace G is the sum of the diagonal entries, so
   trace G = sum_a G_aa = sum_a <v_a, v_a> = sum_a ||D e_a||^2 (real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq).
   By definition this is hsNormSq D = sum_{i : Fin n} ||D (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)||^2.
6. Case n = 0. All sums are empty and G is the empty matrix. So (i) holds by extensionality over the empty index type, the form in (ii) is 0 >= 0, and trace G = 0 = hsNormSq D. Steps 1-5 cover this case verbatim. QED

Lean notes. Checked against the pinned toolchain, using only the contract's imports.
- (i): ext i j; simp only [Matrix.transpose_apply, Matrix.of_apply]; exact real_inner_comm _ _.
- (ii): state the identity of steps 2-3 as a `have`. Prove it by simp only [dotProduct, Matrix.mulVec, Matrix.of_apply, sum_inner, inner_sum, inner_smul_left, inner_smul_right, Finset.mul_sum], then Finset.sum_congr twice, conj_trivial, rw [real_inner_comm (D (EuclideanSpace.single a (1 : ℝ)))] and ring. Finish with real_inner_self_nonneg.
- (iii): simp only [Matrix.trace, Matrix.diag, Matrix.of_apply, hsNormSq, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq].
proof_key_steps: G^T = G entrywise, by symmetry of the real inner product.
x . (G x) = sum_a sum_b x_a x_b <D e_a, D e_b> = <w, w> with w = sum_a x_a D e_a, by bilinearity.
<w, w> >= 0, so G is positive semidefinite.
trace G = sum_a <D e_a, D e_a> = sum_a ||D e_a||^2 = hsNormSq D.
